name: Berkeley
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Berkeley, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Berkeley, CA: Fourth Street lights and Santa's sleigh, Breakfast with Santa at the Tilden carousel, Lawrence Hall Winter Weeks.
lede: Berkeley does Christmas in its shopping streets, its hill parks and its science center: three blocks of lights on Fourth Street, Santa at the century-old Tilden carousel, and a winter break full of experiments at the Lawrence Hall of Science.
celebrates: In west Berkeley, Fourth Street hangs lights in every tree along three blocks and keeps them up into February, sets out a big red Santa mailbox in front of Peet's Coffee, and holds a free craft afternoon with Santa in a wooden sleigh. Up in Tilden Regional Park, the 1911 Tilden Park Merry-Go-Round hosts Breakfast with Santa as part of its Winter Wonderland season. The City of Berkeley's recreation division runs a Pancake Breakfast with Santa at Live Oak Community Center, and the Lawrence Hall of Science, UC Berkeley's public science center, fills the school break with Winter Weeks activities and a New Year's Eve confetti launch.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Berkeley's winter activity guide listed a Tots Winter Carnival at Live Oak on December 6, a Winter Youth Festival at Aquatic Park on December 13 and a Pancake Breakfast with Santa at Live Oak Community Center on Saturday, December 20, with two seatings and tickets at $10 per person. Berkeleyside's December 18 roundup also pointed families to that breakfast and to the Berkeley Path Wanderers Association's festive hike past North Berkeley houses decked in lights.
facts: The Tilden Park Merry-Go-Round was built in 1911 with hand-carved and painted menagerie animals, and it reopened in April 2021 after a restoration. Not far away, the Redwood Valley Railway runs live steam trains on 15-inch gauge track through the redwoods of Tilden Park, with about 1.25 miles of line. Fourth Street's holiday lights come on each night at about 5 pm, and glowing balls of light hang from the branches of the street trees.
trains: Berkeley sits on BART's Richmond line, and the Downtown Berkeley station is the stop for AC Transit bus 67 up to Tilden Park, according to the Tilden carousel. Amtrak's Capitol Corridor stops at Berkeley Station, 700 University Avenue under the University Avenue overpass, a short walk from the Fourth Street shops. In the hills, the Redwood Valley Railway's scale steam trains run in Tilden Regional Park, and Niles Canyon Railway's Train of Lights runs from Sunol and Fremont. Across the Bay, San Francisco's cable cars and historic streetcars run all season.

Winter Holiday Fest and Craft Party
Fourth Street's free craft afternoon brings Santa in a red wooden sleigh, the Grinch, wreath making and glitter pine cones.
Breakfast with Santa at the Tilden carousel
The 1911 Tilden Park Merry-Go-Round serves a buffet breakfast with Santa and his Elf in December.
The City of Berkeley's recreation division hosts a pancake breakfast with Santa and his North Pole friends at Live Oak Community Center.
The Lawrence Hall of Science fills the winter break with science activities and an all-day New Year's Eve confetti launch.
kidfact: The Tilden Park Merry-Go-Round is more than 100 years old. It was built in 1911, and its animals were carved and painted by hand.
faq: Where are the best Christmas lights in Berkeley?

Fourth Street in west Berkeley lights up three blocks every night from about 5 pm, starting at Hearst Avenue. Holiday lights wrap every tree and glowing balls of light hang from the branches, and Fourth Street says the lights stay up until February, so families can stroll them before or after the holidays.
Where can kids see Santa in Berkeley?

Santa sits in a big red wooden sleigh at Fourth Street's free Winter Holiday Fest and Craft Party, eats breakfast with families at the Tilden Park Merry-Go-Round, and joins the City of Berkeley's Pancake Breakfast with Santa at Live Oak Community Center. Each has its own date and booking rules on the host's site.
Is there a Santa mailbox in Berkeley?

Yes. Fourth Street sets up Santa's big red mailbox in front of Peet's Coffee at 1776 Fourth Street. Kids who drop in a letter with a return address before the mid December deadline get a real letter back in the mail from Santa and Mrs. Claus, according to the Fourth Street holiday page.
How do you get to Tilden Park without a car?

The Tilden carousel says AC Transit bus 67 runs to Tilden Park from the Downtown Berkeley BART station. Drivers reach the carousel by Canon Drive, Shasta Road or South Park Drive off Grizzly Peak Boulevard, but South Park Drive closes every winter from November 1 for the newt migration.
What can kids do in Berkeley over winter break?

The Lawrence Hall of Science runs Winter Weeks across the school break, with hands-on activities like building giant molecules and virus models, a free light and shadow play area for ages 2 to 6, a 3D film, and a New Year's Eve confetti launch that lets kids celebrate without staying up late.
